Yes. 

Throughout the story, Ilse is portrayed as a quiet, stoic, but ultimately caring woman—shown especially in how she buys bike lights in bulk to silently protect a local teenager who doesn't take care of his own safety. Because of this maternal instinct, it is a surprising turn at the very end when her phone rings—presumably her son in Munich ("Jonas"), who was foreshadowed in her conversation with Frau Wendt—and she intentionally lets it ring out without answering. 

At the same time, this revelation is entirely appropriate in hindsight. It immediately recontextualizes her extreme brevity when Frau Wendt asked about her son earlier ("Ja"), as well as her quiet melancholy and why she prefers the moments in the middle of the fog where neither shore exists. The twist reframes her kindness toward young Mattis as a potential displacement of affection for an estranged son, making the ending both unexpected and deeply fitting for her character.
